```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# Repository root. Every path below is built from it with file.path(), so the
# chunks work both when knitting and when run one at a time in RStudio.
path <- path.expand("~/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-UCB-O365/Documents/R-Repositories/TVLakes_IceModel")
if (!dir.exists(path)) stop("Repository folder not found: ", path)
# Every plot is also saved as a PNG in figures/Compare_DeltaT_Methods/,
# named after the chunk that makes it (300 dpi).
fig_dir <- file.path(path, "figures", "Compare_DeltaT_Methods")
dir.create(fig_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 10, fig.height = 7,
                      dev = "png", dpi = 150, fig.retina = 2,
                      fig.path = paste0(fig_dir, "/deltaT-"))
```

```{r libraries}
source(file.path(path, "R/functions/libraries.R"))
source(file.path(path, "R/functions/functions.R"))
```

The sensible heat flux in `run_ice_model()` is

*Q~h~ = ρ~air~ · C~a~ · C~h~ · U · ΔT*

where ΔT is the difference between the air and ice-surface temperatures. The
model does not track a separate surface temperature (its top node is held at
the air temperature), so ΔT has to be estimated. This report runs every lake
once per method, **changing nothing but ΔT**, and compares the results.

```{r methods}
method_info <- tibble::tribble(
  ~method,          ~label,             ~surface_temp,                                                       ~colour,
  "lag",            "Lag (original)",   "T_s = previous hour's T_air, so ΔT = T_air(t) − T_air(t−1)",        "#555555",
  "ashton",         "Ashton",           "T_s where conduction through the ice balances air–surface exchange", "#0072B2",
  "lwr_out",        "LWR_out",          "T_s = (LWR_out / εσ)^¼, capped at 0 °C",                             "#E69F00",
  "energy_balance", "Energy balance",   "T_s solved from the full surface energy balance, capped at 0 °C",    "#009E73"
) |>
  dplyr::filter(method %in% params$methods)
methods       <- method_info$method
method_labels <- setNames(method_info$label, method_info$method)
method_cols   <- setNames(method_info$colour, method_info$label)

method_info |>
  dplyr::transmute(`delta_T_method` = paste0("<code>", method, "</code>"),
                   Label = label, `Surface temperature (ΔT = T_air − T_s)` = surface_temp) |>
  knitr::kable(escape = FALSE)
```

Only Q~h~ changes directly. The heat-conduction boundary (top node = T~air~),
the conductive flux Q~c~ and the outgoing longwave are the same for every
method, and the open-water phase at the Rockies lakes is unchanged
(ΔT = T~air~ − T~water~). Every other difference below is a knock-on effect of
Q~h~ through melt and ice thickness.

```{r lakes}
lake_files <- tibble::tribble(
  ~lake_key, ~region,
  "WLB", "McMurdo Dry Valleys", "ELB", "McMurdo Dry Valleys",
  "LH",  "McMurdo Dry Valleys", "LF",  "McMurdo Dry Valleys",
  "GL4", "Colorado Rockies",    "LOC", "Colorado Rockies"
) |>
  dplyr::filter(lake_key %in% params$lakes)
keys        <- lake_files$lake_key
lake_name   <- purrr::map_chr(LAKE_CONFIGS[keys], "lake_name")
lake_levels <- unname(lake_name)
out_dir     <- file.path(path, "Data/model_outputs/deltaT_comparison")
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
out_file    <- function(key, method) file.path(out_dir, sprintf("%s_%s_output.csv", key, method))
```

## Model runs

```{r run, eval = isTRUE(params$rerun)}
keep_cols <- c("time", "thickness", "SW_abs", "LW_net", "sensible_Q", "latent_Q",
               "conductive_Q", "surface_heat_flux", "surface_loss", "bottom_gain",
               "delta_T", "T_surface", "phase")

run_lake <- function(key) {
  old_wd <- setwd(path)                 # the 00_ scripts use repo-relative paths
  on.exit(setwd(old_wd), add = TRUE)
  prep <- new.env(parent = globalenv())
  ok <- tryCatch({
    source(sprintf("R/%s/00_%s_data_preparation.R", key, key), local = prep)
    TRUE
  }, error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))
  if (!isTRUE(ok))
    return(tibble::tibble(lake_key = key, method = methods,
                          status = paste("FAILED (data prep):", ok), minutes = NA_real_))

  ts_ready <- prepare_model_input(prep$inputs$time_series, warming_rate = 0,
                                  constants = lake_constants(key))
  purrr::map_dfr(methods, function(m) {
    message(sprintf("%s: delta_T_method = '%s'", key, m))
    t0  <- Sys.time()
    res <- tryCatch(run_ice_model(ts_ready, constants = lake_constants(key),
                                  show_progress = FALSE, delta_T_method = m),
                    error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))
    mins <- round(as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "mins")), 1)
    if (is.character(res))
      return(tibble::tibble(lake_key = key, method = m, status = paste("FAILED:", res), minutes = mins))
    out <- dplyr::select(res, dplyr::any_of(keep_cols))
    # forcing alongside the output, for the surface-temperature checks below
    forc <- dplyr::select(ts_ready, time, T_air, LWR_out_input = LWR_out)
    out  <- if (nrow(out) == nrow(forc) && all(out$time == forc$time))
      dplyr::bind_cols(out, dplyr::select(forc, -time))
    else dplyr::left_join(out, forc, by = "time")
    readr::write_csv(dplyr::mutate(out, method = m, lake_key = key), out_file(key, m))
    tibble::tibble(lake_key = key, method = m, status = "OK", minutes = mins)
  })
}

run_log <- purrr::map_dfr(keys, run_lake)
```

```{r run-status, eval = isTRUE(params$rerun)}
run_log |>
  dplyr::transmute(Lake = lake_name[lake_key], Method = method_labels[method],
                   Status = status, `Run time (min)` = minutes) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r load}
files <- tidyr::expand_grid(lake_key = keys, method = methods) |>
  dplyr::mutate(file = out_file(lake_key, method)) |>
  dplyr::filter(file.exists(file))
missing <- tidyr::expand_grid(lake_key = keys, method = methods) |>
  dplyr::anti_join(files, by = c("lake_key", "method"))

runs <- purrr::map(files$file, readr::read_csv, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  purrr::map(function(d) { if (!"phase" %in% names(d)) d$phase <- "ice"; d }) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows() |>
  dplyr::mutate(lake  = factor(lake_name[lake_key], levels = lake_levels),
                label = factor(method_labels[method], levels = method_info$label),
                on_ice = phase == "ice" & thickness > 0)
has_runs <- nrow(runs) > 0

if (has_runs) {
  daily <- runs |>
    dplyr::mutate(day = as.Date(time)) |>
    dplyr::group_by(lake_key, lake, method, label, day) |>
    dplyr::summarise(thickness    = mean(thickness),
                     surface_loss = sum(surface_loss),
                     bottom_gain  = sum(bottom_gain),
                     .groups = "drop")

  obs <- purrr::map_dfr(unique(runs$lake_key), function(key) {
    o <- load_ice_observations(key, project_path = path,
                               time_range = range(runs$time[runs$lake_key == key]))
    if (is.null(o) || nrow(o) == 0) return(NULL)
    tibble::tibble(lake_key = key, day = as.Date(o$date_time), obs = abs(o$z_water_m))
  })
  if (nrow(obs) > 0) obs$lake <- factor(lake_name[obs$lake_key], levels = lake_levels)
}

base_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "top")
scale_method <- scale_colour_manual(values = method_cols, name = NULL, drop = TRUE)
```

`r if (!has_runs) "**No ΔT comparison runs found.** Knit with <code>rerun: true</code> to create them." else if (nrow(missing) > 0) sprintf("**Missing runs:** %s. Knit with <code>rerun: true</code> to create them.", paste(lake_name[missing$lake_key], method_labels[missing$method], sep = " / ", collapse = "; ")) else ""`

## Ice thickness

```{r thickness, fig.height = 12, eval = has_runs}
ggplot(daily, aes(day, thickness, colour = label)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.5) +
  { if (nrow(obs) > 0) geom_point(data = obs, aes(day, obs), inherit.aes = FALSE,
                                  colour = "#D6604D", size = 1.4) } +
  scale_method +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y") +
  facet_wrap(~ lake, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Ice thickness (m)",
       title = "Modelled ice thickness with each ΔT method",
       subtitle = "Daily mean; red points = observed depth to water") +
  base_theme
```

```{r thickness-diff, fig.height = 8, eval = has_runs && "lag" %in% methods && length(methods) > 1}
thick_diff <- daily |>
  dplyr::select(lake, day, method, label, thickness) |>
  dplyr::left_join(daily |> dplyr::filter(method == "lag") |>
                     dplyr::select(lake, day, lag = thickness),
                   by = c("lake", "day")) |>
  dplyr::filter(method != "lag") |>
  dplyr::mutate(diff = thickness - lag)

ggplot(thick_diff, aes(day, diff, colour = label)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.5) +
  scale_method +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 years", date_labels = "%Y") +
  facet_wrap(~ lake, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Difference from lag method (m)",
       title = "How much each method changes the modelled thickness",
       subtitle = "Positive = thicker ice than the original (lag) method") +
  base_theme
```

### Fit to observations

```{r fit-table, eval = has_runs && nrow(obs) > 0}
fit <- obs |>
  dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::select(daily, lake_key, day, method, label, model = thickness),
                    by = c("lake_key", "day")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(resid  = model - obs,
                period = ifelse(day < as.Date("2021-07-01"), "Before Jul 2021", "Jul 2021 onward"))
cell <- function(d) dplyr::summarise(d, cell = sprintf("%+.2f / %.2f", mean(resid), sqrt(mean(resid^2))),
                                     rmse = sqrt(mean(resid^2)), n = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop")
fit_tab <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  fit |> dplyr::group_by(lake, label, period) |> cell(),
  fit |> dplyr::group_by(lake, label) |> cell() |> dplyr::mutate(period = "All")
) |>
  dplyr::group_by(lake, period) |>
  dplyr::mutate(cell = ifelse(rmse == min(rmse), paste0("**", cell, "**"), cell)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()
fit_tab |>
  dplyr::mutate(period = factor(period, levels = c("Before Jul 2021", "Jul 2021 onward", "All"))) |>
  dplyr::select(Lake = lake, period, Method = label, cell) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = period, values_from = cell) |>
  dplyr::arrange(Lake, Method) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Model − observed depth to water: bias / RMSE (m). Bold = lowest RMSE for that lake and period.")
```

## ΔT and surface temperature

Monthly means over ice-covered hours. The original (lag) ΔT averages to
almost zero, because it is just the hour-to-hour change in air temperature.
The other methods give a real air-minus-surface difference: negative when the
surface is warmer than the air (heat flows from the ice to the air), positive
when the air is warmer.

```{r monthly}
monthly <- if (has_runs) runs |>
  dplyr::filter(on_ice) |>
  dplyr::mutate(month = lubridate::month(time)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(lake, lake_key, label, month) |>
  dplyr::summarise(delta_T    = mean(delta_T, na.rm = TRUE),
                   T_surface  = mean(T_surface, na.rm = TRUE) - 273.15,
                   T_air      = mean(T_air, na.rm = TRUE) - 273.15,
                   sensible_Q = mean(sensible_Q, na.rm = TRUE),
                   n = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::filter(n >= 24 * 10)
month_axis <- scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = substr(month.abb, 1, 1))
```

```{r delta-T, fig.height = 7, eval = has_runs}
ggplot(monthly, aes(month, delta_T, colour = label)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) + geom_point(size = 1.4) +
  scale_method + month_axis +
  facet_wrap(~ lake, ncol = 3) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "ΔT = T_air − T_s (K)", title = "Monthly mean ΔT") +
  base_theme
```

```{r surface-temp, fig.height = 7, eval = has_runs}
air_line <- monthly |> dplyr::distinct(lake, month, T_air)
ggplot(monthly, aes(month, T_surface, colour = label)) +
  geom_line(data = air_line, aes(month, T_air), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            colour = "grey30", linetype = "22", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) + geom_point(size = 1.4) +
  scale_method + month_axis +
  facet_wrap(~ lake, ncol = 3, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "°C", title = "Monthly mean surface temperature used for ΔT",
       subtitle = "Dashed grey = air temperature") +
  base_theme
```

### Check against measured outgoing longwave (Dry Valley lakes)

At the Dry Valley lakes the outgoing longwave comes from the COHM station, so
it gives an independent surface-temperature estimate,
T~s~ = (LWR~out~ / εσ)^¼. COHM is on Commonwealth Glacier, not on the lakes,
so this is a check on the seasonal pattern and size of T~s~, not an exact
target. (The `lwr_out` method uses this estimate directly, so it matches by
construction. At the Rockies lakes LWR~out~ is a constant, so this check is
skipped there.)

```{r lw-check, eval = has_runs && any(c("WLB", "ELB", "LH", "LF") %in% runs$lake_key)}
eps <- CONSTANTS$emissivity; sig <- CONSTANTS$sigma
lw_check <- runs |>
  dplyr::filter(on_ice, lake_key %in% c("WLB", "ELB", "LH", "LF"), !is.na(T_surface),
                !is.na(LWR_out_input)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(T_s_lw = pmin((LWR_out_input / (eps * sig))^0.25, 273.15),
                err = T_surface - T_s_lw)
lw_check |>
  dplyr::group_by(Lake = lake, Method = label) |>
  dplyr::summarise(`Bias (K)` = mean(err), `RMSE (K)` = sqrt(mean(err^2)),
                   `r (hourly)` = stats::cor(T_surface, T_s_lw), .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Modelled surface temperature vs the LWR_out estimate (hourly, ice-covered)")
```

```{r budget, fig.height = 7, eval = has_runs}
flux_vars <- c(SW_abs = "Absorbed shortwave", LW_net = "Net longwave",

               conductive_Q = "Conductive (−Qc)")
flux_cols <- setNames(c("#E69F00", "#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#009E73", "#CC79A7"), flux_vars)
budget <- runs |>
  dplyr::filter(on_ice) |>

ggplot(budget_long, aes(value, label, fill = flux)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
```


## Surface melt and bottom growth

Totals per ice year (July–June, labelled by the year it ends in).

```{r mass-balance, fig.height = 9, eval = has_runs}
mb <- daily |>
  dplyr::mutate(ice_year = lubridate::year(day) + (lubridate::month(day) >= 7)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(lake, label, ice_year) |>
  dplyr::summarise(`Surface melt` = -sum(surface_loss), `Bottom growth` = sum(bottom_gain),
                   days = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::filter(days >= 300) |>                       # complete ice years only
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(`Surface melt`, `Bottom growth`), names_to = "term", values_to = "m")

ggplot(mb, aes(factor(ice_year), m, fill = label)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.75,
           data = dplyr::filter(mb, term == "Bottom growth")) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.75,
           data = dplyr::filter(mb, term == "Surface melt")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = method_cols, name = NULL) +
  facet_wrap(~ lake, ncol = 2, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "Ice year", y = "m per ice year",
       title = "Annual bottom growth (up) and surface melt (down)") +
  base_theme +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

```{r mb-table, eval = has_runs}
mb |>
  dplyr::group_by(Lake = lake, Method = label, term) |>
  dplyr::summarise(m = mean(m), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = term, values_from = m) |>
  dplyr::mutate(`Net (m/yr)` = `Bottom growth` + `Surface melt`) |>
  dplyr::rename(`Bottom growth (m/yr)` = `Bottom growth`, `Surface melt (m/yr)` = `Surface melt`) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Mean per complete ice year")
```

## Notes

- **Why the Ashton, LWR_out and energy-balance runs can give almost the same
  thickness.** The model only acts on the net surface flux when it is
  positive (surface melt); a negative net flux is discarded, and bottom growth
  depends on the air-temperature-pinned profile, not on Q~h~. So winter
  differences in Q~h~ never reach the ice thickness. During melt, all three
  methods cap T~s~ at 0 °C, so they share the same ΔT = T~air~ − 0 °C and the
  same melt. The lag method is the odd one out because its ΔT is near zero
  during melt too.
- **What differs between methods.** Only ΔT, and so Q~h~, in the ice phase.
  The ice's top node is still set to the air temperature in every run, so the
  conductive flux Q~c~ and the temperature profile respond to T~air~, not to
  the T~s~ each method estimates.
- **Ashton.** T~s~ comes from balancing conduction through the whole ice
  thickness against air–surface exchange (H = ρ~air~ C~a~ C~h~ U), with no
  radiation. Thick ice conducts little, so T~s~ sits close to T~air~ and ΔT
  stays small.
- **LWR_out.** Uses the measured COHM outgoing longwave at the Dry Valley
  lakes. At the Rockies lakes LWR~out~ is a constant (εσT~f~⁴), so T~s~ = 0 °C
  and ΔT = T~air~ − 0 °C, which overstates winter heat loss.
- **Energy balance.** Solves for T~s~ each hour from shortwave, longwave,
  sensible, latent and conduction (linear profile to 0 °C at the ice base),
  with T~s~ capped at 0 °C.
- Raw outputs are in `Data/model_outputs/deltaT_comparison/`.

```{r chi-table}
# Lake settings these runs used (from lake_constants(), so they reflect the
# current R/functions/functions.R)
tibble::tibble(Lake = lake_name,
               `Chi (fraction of SW not absorbed at the surface)` =
                 purrr::map_dbl(keys, ~ lake_constants(.x)$Chi),
               `Ch (sensible transfer coeff.)` = purrr::map_dbl(keys, ~ lake_constants(.x)$Ch)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Settings used by every run in this report")
```
